answers.M8-S1: The author does an experiment to see if his Mason-bees can find their way home after being carried far away, and some of them do.
answers.M8-S2: To show that because the bees were flying low near the ground, the wind got stronger and made it harder for them to get home.
answers.M8-S3: They made it home first and then went back out to get pollen, so the trip was easy for them.
answers.M8-S4: So he could tell which bees were his when they came back to the nest.
answers.M8-S5: When he heads home he is sure the bees will be there, but by the end he isn't sure the experiment worked.
answers.M8-S6: It is told in time order, like a story of the experiment from catching the bees to them coming back.
answers.M8-S7: To show that because the bees stopped to get pollen, they got home really fast, in less than an hour.
answers.M8-S8: Because the bees were hurt and angry, they stung him a lot, so it shows the experiment was hard.
answers.M8-S9: Since they flew low, the breeze got stronger for them and they couldn't see where home was, so getting back was hard.
